analysis:
Examined all four primary analyses and available replayed patches, metadata and changelog source; independently reconciled the visible changes. Replay omits 12 reviewed source units, so the analyses' claims about surrounding controls and routing tests cannot all be directly verified here.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:53-64 adds twelve conditional macOS lanes. The changed runner expressions at head lines 232-234, 477-479, 675-677, 878-880, 1010-1012, 1072-1074 and 1134-1136 consume matching route keys, including independent matrix-shard keys. Counts match the job conditions visible in the patch; the summary retains its dependency on provider shards. docs/developer/build.md's changed routing table and grant description, plus changelog.d/ci-macos-darkbloom-route.md:3-6, describe this same expansion and fallback behavior. These descriptions do not establish actual provisioning or isolation controls. The scripts' changed assertions are represented only by prior analyses/metadata in this replay.

No visible patch changes serving authorization, Apple evidence verification, encryption, plaintext handling, billing, inference implementation or T-041 cache controls. No independently supported gate bypass, credential exposure or security regression qualifies as a finding.

Material uncertainty remains at the newly enabled macOS execution boundary: integration needs the reusable .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and sandbox lifecycle contract to establish runner authenticity, isolation from Mac-owner credentials/live provider data, clean job state, and grant lifetime for the delayed summary job. Verify actual cache/artifact writer trust and separation from signed-release qualification, rather than inferring it from exact labels or documentation. Relevant contracts are ADV-001, A-019, A-017, TB-003 and T-054; TB-011 expressly distinguishes synthetic test success from artifact/host qualification. These controls are outside the supplied evidence, not observed missing controls. Remaining review should target this routing expansion, not re-audit unchanged platform authorization.
